::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

This section is adapted from the multivariate calculus and optimality-condition parts of @zhou2024optim,
used under the MIT License
(see the license text in [Linear Algebra](linear-algebra.qmd#sec-subspaces)).
The source states the second-order Taylor approximation and the optimality conditions without [proof](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof);
here they are proved from the one-variable Taylor theorem,
and the approximation is made exact by evaluating the Hessian at a point between $\vecf{z}$ and $\vecf{z} + \vecf{h}$.
The source calls points with zero gradient critical points;
here they are stationary points,
because the [calculus notes](calculus.qmd#def-critical-point) give "critical point" a wider meaning.
The source states these results for differentiable functions without saying how smooth;
here the first-order results assume continuous first partial derivatives, and the second-order results continuous second partial derivatives.
These parts of the source are not part of this section:

- its remark that maximizing $f$ is minimizing $-f$, and its classification of constraints
- its figure of local, strict local and global minima
- its one-variable Taylor example and its plots
- matrix calculus
- convexity
- Lagrange multipliers
- Newton's method and gradient descent

:::
